text: After this you can explain what a support decision study should decide and deliver.

For education only; this is not legal, purchasing, financial or safety advice. This lesson uses support analysis to answer a practical question: which arrangement can keep equipment usable for the tasks that matter? Begin with the result users need, not a preferred supplier. The study considers people, spare parts, facilities, information, costs and agreements as one system. It ends in an explained recommendation, subject to the real decision owner’s approval.

items: Inferred: A group needs a set of devices ready for daily operations. The decision is how to maintain usable devices, not whether to select one named supplier.

text: Establish the need, measure current support, compare alternatives, then select a recommended model.
Define the needed result before favouring a delivery partner.
A mandatory constraint can narrow the choices; it should still be made explicit.
